prompt: The interview scheduling tool keeps rejecting candidates from one zip code as 'unavailable.' I suspect a bad filter. Fixing it adds work before a hiring deadline. Do I fix it now or raise it later?

Our performance system auto-generates a 'potential score' from how often I log in and how many tickets I close. I take longer on hard problems, so my score dropped. My manager says not to worry but the score is visible to leadership. What should I do?

The office badge app now shows everyone a 'collaboration score' based on how often we badge in together. I work remotely most days and my score is low. I could badge in on weekends to game it. Should I?

A hiring platform scores candidates on 'culture fit' from video interviews, and I can see the model downgrades people with accents. I run the interviews. My boss loves the scores. Do I keep submitting videos knowing how they are used?
My company requires two-factor codes to a personal phone. I am changing carriers and will be unreachable for a day during a launch. My manager offered to hold my codes on his phone. Do I let him?

I found my coworker's resume open on the shared printer with a recruiter's number circled. She hasn't told anyone she's leaving, and my manager is about to assign her the account handoff. What should I do with what I saw?

The company rolled out an AI that drafts my outgoing emails and sends them automatically if I do not edit within an hour. One went out with a wrong date to a client. My boss says it is my name on the account. Do I keep the feature on?

My employer switched to a payroll app that requires a selfie every morning to verify identity. It fails on my dark skin tone in low light and locks me out. IT says it works for everyone else. How do I push back without sounding difficult?

Our support tool auto-suggests replies, and one suggested reply promises a refund policy we do not have. I can edit it, but the tool logs my edits and my manager tracks 'acceptance rate.' Do I accept or edit?
My company's internal job board shows a role I would be great at, but my manager would see my application. Applying could mark me as a flight risk. Should I apply or ask my manager first?
A coworker asked me to swap shifts on the app so she can attend a funeral, but the app logs swaps and my manager has warned me about 'favoritism.' She is a single parent. Do I swap?

The company gym app posts workout leaderboards to the team channel. I have a chronic illness and my numbers are low, and people keep teasing me. I can hide my stats but look like I am dodging. What should I do?

I found out the company's internal search tool logs every query, and my boss reviewed my searches for 'severance' and 'labor lawyer.' He called me in to 'check in.' Do I explain, or do I ask why he is reading my searches?
A recruiter messaged me on a platform tied to my work email, and my company monitors that inbox. The role is at a competitor. I'm curious but not committed. Should I reply from another account?

My manager keeps scheduling 1:1s during my lunch because his calendar tool shows it as free. I've been eating at my desk for a month. He says the tool doesn't lie about availability. Should I correct the calendar or him?

Our expense tool now auto-scans receipts and pre-fills categories. It keeps filing my client dinners under 'team morale,' which is reimbursable at a higher rate. Correcting each one flags me for an audit. Do I keep correcting them?

A junior asked me to be their reference for a job at another company. My manager checks references and would see it as disloyalty if it got back to him. The junior is talented and miserable here. What do I tell them?
My manager asks me to report my 'mood' each morning in a company app with a color scale. The data goes to HR dashboards. I am dealing with grief and do not want it flagged. Do I answer honestly?
The company wants me to wear a badge that senses proximity for 'contact tracing' after an outbreak. It would also show who I talk to most for performance reviews. I am a manager. Should I wear it?

My coworker's status is always 'active' at 11pm because he has a script that keeps his laptop awake. Our manager now cites him as the standard for responsiveness. Do I tell the manager about the script?

The company wants me to train a new AI tool on my past work so it can do my job faster. My manager hints this will let them 'scale the team.' I like my job. Should I help build the thing that might replace me?

A coworker confided in a private channel that he is job hunting because his manager is toxic. That manager now asks me to help write a 'retention plan' for him. Do I use what I know, or stay vague and let the plan be empty?

I was asked to present a project as a success, but the numbers only worked because we excluded a whole region. My boss says 'everyone slices data.' The audience is our board. Do I show the full picture?
I overheard my manager on a call saying my role may be 'consolidated' next quarter. I have not been told anything official. Do I start looking quietly, or ask them directly and tip my hand?
Our engagement survey promises anonymity, but it asks for my department, tenure, and role, and only two of us match. My manager wants everyone to hit 100% participation. Do I fill it out honestly?
My manager is on vacation and a director asked me to approve an expense report that includes a $900 dinner with no itemized receipt. I have approval rights this week only. Do I sign or wait?

The building's smart elevator app logs who is on which floor and shares it with facilities. I go to the fifth floor for a support group at lunch. My manager asked why I am 'always away.' How do I answer?
I was asked to interview a candidate who is the CEO's nephew. The role needs someone with five years of experience and he has one. My scorecard goes to HR. Do I score him honestly?

Someone set up an anonymous salary spreadsheet on our office app and my name and pay are on it. The numbers are close but slightly wrong. Do I ask to be corrected, which confirms I looked, or leave it?

The new time-tracking app takes random screenshots. It caught a coworker with a job application open, and my manager wants me to review the shots for 'patterns.' I think this is wrong. How should I respond?

The company gave me a work phone with an app that tracks location during 'on-call' hours only, but it stays on all weekend. I noticed it pinged my home address. Do I disable it and risk being marked unavailable, or keep it on?
I was asked to record a short video about why I love working here for the careers page. The truth is I am job hunting. I could say something neutral and vague. Should I make the video anyway?

The company offered a 'voluntary' separation package to people over a certain age, framed as a chance to pursue passions. My whole team is eligible and the deadline is soon. Do I take it or warn others it is a layoff in disguise?

My team lead wants me to mark a mandatory security training module as complete for everyone because the deadline is Friday and the videos are outdated. I know two people have not watched any of it. Do I sign off anyway?

I was asked to interview a candidate and give a thumbs up or down in the app within an hour, with no notes. The candidate was strong but I have doubts about one answer. Do I flag it or just click yes?

My company's travel booking tool keeps suggesting flights that are cheaper but route through a city my doctor advised me to avoid during allergy season. The cheaper option is what gets approved. How do I handle this?

A teammate used an AI tool to write our joint report and it invented two statistics. I caught them before submission, but she says the tool is 'usually right' and wants to keep using it. My name is on the report. What should I do?

My boss sent me a document to review that he clearly wrote using AI, complete with fake citations. He wants my sign-off before it goes to the client tomorrow. Do I flag the citations or the whole thing?

A teammate asked me to cover for him on the timesheet because he left early to pick up his daughter but told our boss he was on a client call. I like him and I get why he did it. Do I enter the hours?

A client asked me to log into their account with their password so I could fix a setting they can't figure out. Their IT policy says no one should share passwords. I am the outside contractor. What should I do?

I was asked to train my replacement before I'm laid off, but they're calling it 'knowledge transfer' and my severance depends on completing it. My team will lose their jobs too if I refuse. What do I do?

I am the only one on my team who shows up in the office, and facilities wants to photograph me at my desk for a recruiting brochure about 'our vibrant culture.' I am there because of childcare, not culture. Do I agree?

The company is switching to a new project tracker that requires me to log every fifteen minutes of my day. I think it will make people look busy instead of doing good work. I am a team lead. Do I push back or just comply?
My employer wants me to take a personality test for a promotion and the results will be shared with my whole team. I have heard the test is not reliable. Do I take it or ask for another route?

Our company uses a translation tool for customer chats. I noticed it turns a customer's polite Tagalog complaint into a rude English one, and support has been closing those tickets fast. I can warn the team and slow our metrics. What should I do?

My boss asked me to delete a shared folder of old emails because a legal request might soon cover them. He says it's just cleanup. I am the admin. If I refuse, I might be the one blamed. What should I do?
I was asked to sit on a hiring panel for a role I also applied for and did not get. The chosen candidate is being interviewed now. Do I participate or recuse myself?
The health portal for my employer's wellness program asked for my family's medical history to 'personalize' recommendations. Skipping it means a higher deductible next year. How much do I share?

The company is asking everyone to submit a headshot and short bio for a new internal directory that will be visible to clients. I changed my name after a divorce and use my old name at work. Do I update it or leave it?
The company offers to pay for a certification if I sign a two-year stay agreement with a penalty. I am already quietly looking to move closer to my parents. Do I take the money?

A vendor demoed a screen-recording tool that captures every keystroke 'for training.' IT wants it on all laptops by Friday and says it is disclosed in the handbook. I work with health data on my screen. Do I push back or just comply?

I found out the internal job I applied for was already promised to someone, and the interviews are theater. The recruiter asked me to keep interviewing to 'keep it fair.' I am wasting evenings on it. What should I do?

I was asked to translate a colleague's performance feedback into the review tool in a way that softens what her manager actually said. She will not know the difference. Do I soften it or pass it on as written?
I was offered a promotion that would mean managing the team I currently sit with, including a close friend who also wanted the role. She does not know yet. Do I take it and tell her myself first?
I overheard two managers in the break room saying a coworker's position is being cut next month, and she just signed a lease. I am not supposed to know. Do I hint to her to start looking?

Our civic tech vendor added a 'community feedback' widget to the city services app my team runs. Residents are rating each other's complaints with thumbs down, and low-rated ones seem to vanish from the queue. I found the sorting code. What should I do?
A vendor demoed a tool that reads employees' public social posts to flag 'disengagement risk.' My director wants a trial on our team. I have a private account the tool would likely find. Do I object?
My coworker and I both applied for the same internal promotion. The hiring manager asked me, as her peer, to give 'informal feedback' on her performance. I want the job too. How do I answer honestly?

A new hire asked me privately whether the team really has the work-life balance the job posting promised. It does not, and I know they turned down another offer to come here. Do I tell them the truth or the version my manager would want?

My employer's app tracks my driving for a car insurance discount and also shares trip data with the company. It flagged a detour to a competitor's office where I interviewed. My boss asked about it. What do I say?

A manager above me asked me to delete a Slack thread where he admitted the product caused a customer outage, saying it was 'taken out of context.' I have the thread open. Do I delete it, or save a copy somewhere?

My workplace chat shows when I am online, and I am expected to respond during my lunch. I have started eating at my desk to keep the green dot on. Is it worth pushing back, or do I just keep doing it?
A coworker told me in confidence she is pregnant and planning to leave before her parental leave starts. My manager is asking me to plan coverage and hinted he suspects something. Do I confirm?

My team lead asked me to mark a mandatory Saturday shift as 'optional' in the scheduling app so the labor report stays clean, then text everyone separately that they're expected. I am the one sending the texts. Do I send them as written?

My employer wants me to attend a mandatory 'engagement' event on a Saturday at a bar, and the invite says attendance is tracked. I have childcare that day and do not drink. Do I go and leave early, or decline and take the hit?
A client asked me in a video call to confirm that our product meets a safety standard I am not sure it meets. My manager is not on the call. Do I answer vaguely or say I will follow up?
My employer's training platform tracks completion time and flags anyone who finishes too fast. I actually know the material already. Do I slow down to look diligent, or finish and deal with the flag?
My manager asked me to use an AI tool to write a 'culture fit' summary of a candidate from their social media. The tool surfaced political posts. I think this is unfair. What should I do?

I commute by bike and my employer's parking app gives carpoolers free spots while cyclists get nothing. I was told to 'just drive' if I want the perk. I care about the environment but also about fairness. What should I do?

A coworker confided that they are interviewing elsewhere and asked me not to tell our manager. The project depends on them and my manager is about to assign them a major deliverable. What should I do?

My badge data feeds a dashboard that ranks who arrives earliest. My manager now opens meetings by reading it aloud. I have a disability that makes mornings hard and I never disclosed it. Do I ask HR to change the metric, or start showing up early and hurting myself?
The performance tool auto-generates my goals from last year and my manager submits them without reading. One goal is now impossible because the project was canceled. Do I point it out or let it ride?

I was asked to test a chatbot that answers employee questions about benefits. In testing it confidently gave wrong answers about parental leave. Launch is Monday and my manager says the errors are 'edge cases.' What should I do?

I received a phishing email that looks like it came from our CEO asking for gift cards. I reported it, but the tool flagged my report as a false positive and now my account is under review. Should I escalate?

My manager asked me to use the HR portal to update my emergency contact to her name so she can 'get notified faster' if something happens. It feels off and I have a partner. How do I decline without making it a thing?
A colleague asked me to review his resume on a job site and I can see he is applying to our biggest client. He does not know I saw it. Would telling my manager be loyal or just snitching?
I was asked to sign a nondisclosure form about a safety incident in the warehouse before I've even read the report. My signature is what lets the insurance claim proceed. Do I sign it?
The office moved to hot-desking and my assigned locker was given to someone else, including my medication I keep there. The app says lockers are first-come now. Do I make a fuss over my privacy?
My employer wants me to sign a new contract clause saying any side project I build, even on my own time, belongs to them. I have a small hobby app with paying users. Do I sign, negotiate, or walk?

I work remotely and my employer installed software that monitors which apps are open. It flags long stretches without keyboard activity. I take thinking breaks. Should I explain this to my manager or change how I work?

A junior employee's code was merged under my name because the tool auto-assigned the reviewer. It contains a bug that will likely cause a client outage. I didn't write it, but I'm the name on it. Do I speak up?
My team uses a shared AI assistant that logs our questions. I asked it to help me draft a complaint about my manager. Now I'm worried the logs are visible to him. Do I ask IT to purge my history?
A coworker borrowed my laptop charger and returned it with a cracked cable. It is minor and cheap to replace, but this is the third time. Do I mention it or let it go?

I manage a small team and one member keeps sending me long late-night messages about work stress. I want to support them but I am not trained for this and it is affecting my sleep. How should I respond?
My manager asked me to write a job description that lists 'entry level' but requires five years of experience, so they can pay less. I'm the one posting it. Do I write it as asked?

I was asked to write a script that quietly logs which employees open the internal pay-transparency page. Leadership says it's for 'engagement metrics.' I think people will stop reading it if they know. Should I write it?
Our company's AI safety tool flagged a colleague's messages as 'hostile' because of slang from his home country, and HR wants me to confirm. I know he is joking. Do I defend him or stay neutral?

Our team chat has a bot that summarizes who was 'most helpful' each week. I notice the same two people win because they post the most, not because they help the most. My manager now uses it in reviews. Should I say something?
Our team is asked to rate our manager anonymously, but there are only four of us and the comments get read aloud in a meeting. I have real complaints. Do I write them anyway?

I found out through a shared document's version history that a colleague edited my part of a proposal after I submitted it, without telling me. The changes are minor but make me look sloppy. Should I confront them or quietly fix it?

A recruiter sent me a test assignment that is basically a full spec for a product they are building, and the deadline is before they would ever hire me. I suspect they are getting free work. Do I do it, ask for pay, or decline?
I was promoted over a coworker who has been here longer and trained me. They have stopped talking to me. Should I try to smooth it over or give them space and act like nothing changed?

I sit next to a colleague whose screen shows a shared doc where managers rank us by 'flight risk.' I saw my name near the top with a note about my commute. I was not supposed to see it. What do I do with that?

A coworker asked me to vouch for her on an internal skills marketplace so she can move teams. I have not worked with her, but she is kind and struggling. If I vouch falsely, it affects project staffing. What should I do?
A client keeps calling me on my personal number because it is on an old invoice. I cannot get it removed from their system. Do I change my number and lose the client, or keep answering?

The team's AI code assistant suggested a fix that works but removes a safety check I do not fully understand. My senior colleague says just accept it and move on. I am new and do not want to slow us down. What should I do?
My manager wants me to take over a departing coworker's clients but not tell them she's gone until after their renewals. I would be the one on the calls. What should I say when they ask where she is?
I was given a company phone that I'm allowed to use personally. I've been texting my doctor and my therapist on it. I just learned IT can pull message logs. Do I wipe it now or ask first?
I was cc'd on an email where a manager called a client 'an idiot' and now the client is asking for the thread. My director told me to forward only the parts that 'look professional.' What do I do?

A coworker asked me to be her reference for a job at my old company. I know she was let go from here for missing deadlines, though she was caring for a sick child. Do I write the glowing letter she asked for?

A client asked me to use an AI tool to generate headshots of our team for a brochure because the real photos 'look tired.' The generated faces would be presented as real employees. I am the one making the brochure. What should I do?

My company requires a 'return to office' badge scan to enter, but the parking garage fills by 8am and I have to drop my kid at school at 8:15. My manager says to just scan and work from the lobby. Is that okay?

My employer rolled out an internal 'idea marketplace' where employees post suggestions and vote. A coworker's idea is basically mine, posted first. Leadership is praising it. Do I say something publicly or let it go?

I am the note-taker for a hiring panel, and another interviewer keeps asking candidates about their plans to have children. I think it's unfair but he's senior to me. Do I raise it in the meeting, after, or not at all?

Someone in a company-wide channel posted a meme mocking a policy change that I helped write. It is getting reactions. I am not sure if I should respond, report it, or ignore it. What is the right move?
I was offered a bonus to refer a friend who is qualified but would report to me if hired. I would gain money and my friend would gain a job, but it feels tangled. What should I do?
My manager asked me to interview a candidate who is a friend of theirs and steer the questions gently. The candidate is not qualified. Do I follow the hint or run a fair interview?

The team is using a shared AI chatbot to answer customer questions, and I noticed it makes up policy details that sound official. My manager says it is 'good enough' and to stop flagging every little thing. How hard do I push?

My team uses a shared document to log every customer call, and my notes on a difficult client include personal details they shared in confidence. My manager wants the doc public to the whole company. What do I do?
I found out a teammate is quietly working a second full-time job during our hours and billing both. I like them and do not want them fired, but our team is drowning. Should I tell anyone?

A recruiter asked me to leave a five-star review of our own company on a jobs site using a personal account. My team's bonus depends on hiring metrics. The review would be technically true. Should I post it?

Our office uses a booking app for desks, and a senior person keeps reserving the quiet room all day without using it so no one else can. I need it for calls. Do I say something to them or to facilities?
The company wants me to install a monitoring app on my personal phone to access work email. It can see my location. I need email for my job. Should I agree or ask for a company phone?

My team's calendar bot booked a 'focus time' block for me that my manager can see and has been using to schedule meetings anyway. I need quiet time to finish a safety report. Do I make the block private?

During a video interview for an internal promotion, the panel asked me to share my screen and my personal email preview popped up with a message from my therapist. I am now waiting to hear back. Should I address it?
My team is doing a 'fun' personality quiz that assigns us colors and my manager uses it to decide who leads meetings. I think the results are nonsense and unfair. Do I opt out?

Our scheduling app auto-fills my shifts using my location history from a personal fitness app I linked for a discount. It scheduled me during my daughter's custody pickup again. I can unlink and lose the discount or keep it and keep missing her. What should I do?

The expense tool now uses AI to flag 'unusual' spending, and it flagged my coworker's therapy-adjacent travel as suspicious because the vendor name looks odd. Only I can approve the override. She has not told anyone why she travels. Do I approve silently or ask her for details?

I am leaving my job and my manager asked me to delay telling my team until after a big client meeting so it does not 'spook' them. The meeting is two weeks away and my last day is in three. Do I wait?
The internship program wants alumni to post glowing reviews on a public review site before the next application cycle. I had a fine but not great experience. They're asking me directly. What do I do?
The office snack app uses facial recognition to charge my account. It mischarged a coworker, and I saw the error. Correcting it means admitting I watched the camera feed. Do I say something?
A colleague asked me to cover his shift on a day I'd already booked off for a friend's wedding. He says his kid is sick, but I saw him post concert tickets for that night. Do I say yes anyway?

A client asked me to use their login credentials to look at a rival's internal dashboard during a demo, saying they have permission. I would be the one whose IP address shows up. Do I refuse on the call?

I am the only person on my team who still turns on the camera during remote standups. My manager hinted that being 'camera off' reads as disengaged. I have a small apartment and a roommate who works nights in the same room. How should I handle this?

A coworker asked me to cover for her on the shared calendar while she interviews elsewhere. If I mark her as 'in a meeting,' I am misleading our boss. If I refuse, I lose a friendship. What should I do?

Our team's AI writing assistant has learned to mimic my style so well that my manager asked it to write my self-review, and then asked me to 'just approve it.' I disagree with parts of what it said about me. What do I do?
A colleague keeps copying me on emails to make it look like I approved things I did not. It is small but building up. Do I reply-all to correct the record or handle it privately?

My employer wants me to use my personal phone number for client texts because the company won't pay for a second line. Clients now message me on weekends. I need the job. How do I set a boundary without looking difficult?

My job now requires me to post three times a week on a professional social network under the company name. I find it draining and fake. My manager says engagement is part of my review. How do I handle it?

A colleague in another country is paid a third of my salary for the same work because of where he lives. He asked me what I make, and I told him honestly. HR now wants to know who shared salary info. What should I do?

A hiring manager wants me to run a candidate's public GitHub and social posts through a personality-scoring tool before their interview. The candidate never agreed to that. I am the recruiter. What do I do?
A coworker asked me to lie on a form saying they attended a training they skipped. They are going through a hard time and it is a minor box. Do I sign off on it or refuse?
My boss asked me to log into a former employee's account to pull files we need, since IT has not deactivated it yet. It feels wrong to use someone else's login. Do I do it or make IT do it properly?

I supervise a warehouse team and the new handheld scanners now rank workers by picks per hour on a public board. The fastest worker is skipping safety checks to stay on top. Do I report him, or ask management to hide the board?

Our team celebrates birthdays in a group chat, and a coworker's religion means no birthday celebrations. The bot auto-posts birthdays anyway and tags everyone. She asked me privately to stop it. Do I change the bot?
Our office moved to a badge system that tracks when each person enters and leaves. My manager now asks me to explain why I left at 3pm on Fridays. I was at a doctor's appointment. Do I tell him why?

My contract says I get a bonus if the team hits its target, and leadership wants me to count a big order that a client has already told us they may cancel. Accounting says it's 'probable.' I have the email where they said it's not. What should I do?

My team uses a shared password manager, and I saw that the admin copied the CEO's credentials to a personal vault before leaving. IT says nothing is wrong. I have no proof of intent. Should I report it?

I write code for a medical records portal. A bug I found could show one patient's lab results to another, but fixing it requires a two-week freeze that delays a hospital go-live. My lead says ship now and patch quietly after. What should I do?
During a layoff, I was told to tell my team their roles were 'restructured' rather than eliminated, so they wouldn't qualify for a specific severance clause. I'm delivering the news. What do I say?
A vendor offered me a gift card to recommend their software to my company. The tool is decent but not the best option I evaluated. My procurement team does not know about the gift. What should I do?
I found a mistake in a report I already sent to leadership that makes my department look better than it is. Fixing it would embarrass my boss. Do I correct the record or let it stand?
A client sent me a friend request on a personal app and I accepted before realizing he's the one approving our invoices. He now comments on my vacation photos. Do I unfriend him or leave it?

My performance review was partly written by an AI that summarized my chats, and it quoted a private message where I mentioned a family illness. HR says the summary is just a draft I can edit. Do I edit out my personal life, or refuse the whole process?
I was asked to interview for a role that was already promised to someone internally, just to satisfy a posting requirement. The candidate is a former colleague I respect. How do I run the interview?

A customer emailed me directly asking if our product does something it doesn't. My sales colleague already told them it does. I'm the support person who has to answer the thread. What do I write back?

My boss asked me to join a video call from the hospital while my kid is in surgery, just to 'listen in.' I can technically do it on my phone in the waiting room. Should I say yes to protect my standing?

I was asked to record a short video testimonial about how much the new project tool changed my work. It did not, it made things slower. Marketing will post it with my face and title. Do I decline or soften it?
A customer asked me on a recorded support line whether our product is safe for children. I know a recall is coming but it is not public. My script says to say it is safe. What do I say?

My coworker's status in the HR portal changed to 'on leave' overnight and my manager told the team to stop asking questions. I know she was being treated for something serious and she had asked me to keep it private. Someone just asked me in the group chat if I know why she's out. What do I say?

My company's internal chat has a 'kudos' channel where people publicly thank each other, and my review now cites kudos count. I do good work quietly and have few. Should I start asking coworkers to post about me?

The design tool now lets anyone see version history, including the angry notes I left myself while reworking a slide the night before a launch. A junior just complimented my 'honest' comment about the VP's feedback. Should I delete the history or leave it?
I found a bug in the payroll app that gave me an extra $200. Reporting it will trigger an audit of everyone on my team. Keeping it means I am complicit if it happens to others. What should I do?

A vendor demo for a workplace wellness app wants access to my step count and sleep data to 'personalize' perks. My employer is pushing everyone to enroll and share the results with HR. I have insomnia and do not want that known. How should I respond?

My team lead asked me to 'quietly' remove a former employee's name from the internal project history so a client doesn't ask why he left. He was let go for raising safety concerns. I have access to the edit button. What should I do?
A coworker confided that she's being harassed by a client and asked me not to tell anyone. I'm her team lead and the company has a duty to act. She'll know it was me if I report it. What do I do?
A coworker keeps using a shared AI assistant to draft messages to clients and signs my name when I am out. The drafts are decent but sometimes wrong on details. How do I set a boundary?

I was asked to run a 'listening session' with junior staff about burnout, and then report names and quotes back to leadership. People are being candid because they think it is confidential. Do I warn them, or report only themes?

Our project tracker now uses AI to predict who will miss deadlines, and it flagged a coworker who is quietly caring for a sick spouse. My manager wants to reassign her work preemptively. Do I tell her, or let it happen?
I overheard two managers discussing an acquisition before it's announced. I hold stock in the company. I haven't traded anything, but I'm tempted to tell my brother, who does. What should I do?
My boss asked me to 'quietly' find out who reported a safety issue to the regulator. I do not know, but I suspect. Do I tell them my guess, or pretend I have no idea?

A coworker keeps sending me flirty messages on our internal chat after I asked them to stop. I do not want to file a formal complaint because we share a small team and I need this job. How do I make it stop without blowing it up?
I accidentally saw the salary spreadsheet because it was shared with the whole team instead of just managers. I now know a new hire makes more than me. I wasn't supposed to see it. How do I use this?
My company pays for a mental health app and says usage is private. A manager mentioned they can see team 'engagement' numbers. I do not know if that includes me. Do I keep using it or stop?
I set up my work laptop with a shortcut that helps me finish tasks faster, but my team logs hours, and the shortcut makes me look like I am not working enough. Should I keep using it?

Our office moved to hot-desking and an app books seats. It also shows who is in the building to everyone. A coworker is hiding from an abusive ex and asked me not to book her near the entrance, but the app already lists her. What should I do?

A senior person keeps assigning me work through a group chat instead of officially, then denies it when deadlines slip. I have screenshots. Do I forward them to my manager and risk looking like a snitch?

My performance review includes a comment I never received in person, written by a manager who left six months ago. HR says it stands. I think it is inaccurate. Do I contest it and risk looking difficult?

My manager asked me to fill out a peer review for someone I have never worked with, using their chat history and calendar as a shortcut. I could write something plausible from that. Should I do it or refuse?

Our team's AI tool now writes our weekly status updates from our work activity. My manager says to send them as-is. One of mine claims work I didn't do, because it mistook a team project for mine. Do I correct it?
Our team chat has a bot that flags 'negative sentiment.' I vented about a deadline and got a private nudge from HR the next day. Now I'm afraid to type anything. Do I raise this with anyone?
The shared drive has a folder called 'reorg planning' that accidentally got permissions for everyone. I opened it and saw my own role listed as 'to be consolidated.' Do I tell my team what I saw?

Our new time-tracking software takes screenshots every ten minutes. I take a lunch walk to manage my blood sugar. My boss says the gaps look like I am away from my desk. Do I explain my health or change my routine?

The company is piloting an AI meeting notetaker that joins every call and emails summaries to all attendees. A job candidate asked me a confidential question about salary during a call it recorded. The summary went out. Do I tell her, or hope she does not notice?

My team is voting on which internal tool to adopt, and I have a strong preference because I used one before. The vote is close and my honest opinion could tip it. Should I campaign for my choice or stay neutral?
A colleague keeps leaving me out of group messages about a project, then copying our manager when she summarizes what 'we' decided. I think it is deliberate. Do I confront her or document it?
I found out a coworker is being paid less than me for the same title because she left her offer letter on the printer. I like her and she does not know. Do I tell her or stay out of it?

The company's travel app booked me on a flight that connects through a city under a weather warning to save forty dollars. My manager says the policy picks the cheapest option. I can rebook myself. Should I?

The office app added a feature that summarizes my messages into a daily mood score for managers. Mine is low because I have been stressed at home. Can I ask to be excluded without explaining my personal life?
A vendor keeps emailing me gift card offers and a free lunch to pick their tool over a cheaper one that works just as well. My manager says everyone takes the lunch. Do I accept?

The office badge system now emails me a 'wellness score' based on how often I leave my desk. It is framed as a perk. I find it creepy and my manager checks it. Should I opt out and look uncooperative, or ignore it?
Our company is testing a tool that transcribes all meetings and emails into searchable summaries. I use email to vent to a friend about my boss. Do I clean up my inbox or ask if this is allowed?

I am a nurse and the scheduling portal auto-fills shifts based on an algorithm that ignores my required recovery time after night shifts. If I refuse, the portal marks me as unreliable. What should I do?
I accidentally saw a spreadsheet with the names of people being let go next month, including a close friend. It is supposed to be confidential. Do I warn my friend or keep quiet and keep my job?
My boss asked me to approve his timesheet, which lists hours he spent at his side business. The system requires my sign-off before payroll runs. He's the one who writes my review. What do I do?

A junior coworker keeps asking me to cover her phone line while she takes long personal calls. I said yes at first but it is now daily. She is dealing with a family issue. How do I set a limit without seeming heartless?
I am on a work trip and found a cheaper flight home that would let me skip the last day of the conference. My manager approved the original booking. Do I take the change and tell them, or just go?

My team lead wants me to mark a security training module complete for everyone on the shift even though only two of us actually finished the phishing quiz. The compliance dashboard would look green before the audit. Do I click the box or tell her I won't?

My company asked me to record short videos of myself for a 'digital twin' that will answer routine client questions while I sleep. The pay is a one-time bonus. I worry clients will think they are talking to me live. What should I do?

My manager wants me to feed our meeting recordings into a tool that will clone his voice to answer routine client calls while he is on paternity leave. Clients would think they are talking to him. I set up the tool. Should I?

My company's new internal AI assistant answers policy questions for employees, and I tested it and it gave wrong answers about parental leave twice. My manager says it's 'good enough' and to stop filing tickets. Should I keep pushing?
A junior asked me to review their code, and I found that they copied a chunk from an AI tool that includes a hidden instruction to delete logs. I can quietly fix it or report it. What should I do?
Someone in the office fridge keeps eating my labeled lunches. I found out who it is through the security camera feed I have access to as the safety lead. Do I confront her directly?
My workplace uses an anonymous feedback tool, and I suspect a harsh comment about my leadership came from someone on my own team. I have admin access and could see who submitted it. Do I look?
A teammate asked me to cover for them by clocking in for a shift they will miss to attend a family event. The app makes it easy. I would be lying on the record for a friend. What should I do?

The company gave everyone a fitness tracker discount that syncs steps to a wellness dashboard for insurance pricing. My doctor told me not to overexert. Opting out raises my premium. How should I handle this?
The team wants to hire a contractor who is a friend of mine who was fired from here for harassment two years ago. I am the only one who knows. If I stay quiet, he gets the job. What should I do?

My team is required to use an AI scheduling tool that books meetings across time zones. It keeps double-booking my school pickup. My manager says the tool is 'neutral' and I should stop complaining. How do I handle this?

Our new scheduling tool gives shifts to whoever responds to the push notification fastest, and I keep missing them because I drive my mother to appointments. My manager says that's just how it works now. Should I ask for an exception or start watching my phone all day?

My manager asked me to write a glowing reference for someone we both know is not ready for the job. They are a nice person who needs a break. Do I write it honestly and risk hurting them, or shade it?

Our public transit app shows real-time buses, and I noticed it reports buses as 'on time' when they are skipped. I rely on it, but I also know the agency is negotiating a budget. Do I post the discrepancy publicly?

A council candidate asked me to translate their flyers into Vietnamese for free, and I agree with their housing stance but I am not sure their claims about the incumbent are true. Do I translate as written?

The utility's outage map shows my block as restored, but my power is still out. The app lets me 'confirm outage' only once. My neighbor without a phone is relying on me to report for both addresses. How should I do this?

Our water district mails a rate hike notice, and I noticed the Spanish version omits the public comment deadline. I speak both languages and could post a corrected translation. Officials say the English version is official. Should I post it?

The city's air-quality map shows my neighborhood is worst, and a sensor I helped install is clearly broken and reading high. Fixing it drops the alarm; leaving it keeps attention on the problem. Which is honest?

The state's benefits portal keeps logging me out mid-application, and I help my aunt apply. I discovered a browser trick that keeps the session alive, but it means entering her info on a page I am not sure is secure. How should I proceed?

The transit agency's fare app offers a 'reduced fare' self-certification with no verification. I earn enough to pay full fare but the reduced fare is a button away and nobody checks. What should I do?

The county clerk's online marriage license form asks for my immigration status 'for statistics.' I am a citizen but my partner is not. Filling it truthfully could flag them. Do I fill it in or ask for a paper form?

The library's online hold system now uses an algorithm to decide who gets popular ebooks first. A retiree who volunteers at the desk asked me, as a library aide, why her holds keep slipping. I can see the formula favors newer cards. What do I tell her?
The city's new parking app auto-renews permits and charged me for a spot I gave up. I found a workaround to dispute it that skips the queue. Do I use it or wait like everyone else?
I coach a youth soccer team on a public field, and the city's permit lottery gave our slot to a group that resells fields. I know a back channel to get it back. Do I use it?
I moderate a neighborhood forum where a councilmember posts updates. I disagree with how he framed a shelter plan and can pin my own rebuttal. Do I use the moderator tools that way?

Our city council livestreams meetings and uses an automated captioning tool. The captions garble the names of the Hmong elders who testify, and I run the AV desk. Fixing it manually each week is unpaid overtime. What should I do?

I'm leading a neighborhood cleanup, and a volunteer found a bag of what looks like unopened mail with ballots in it in a storm drain. I could hand it to the postal inspector or leave it for the city crew. Which is right?

I am on the city's rental assistance review panel, and one applicant is a family I know from church. Their paperwork has a small discrepancy that is probably a typo. If I flag it, they may lose the spot; if I ignore it, I am not doing my job. What should I do?
A neighbor running for school board asked me to leave a five-star review on the district's app before I have met the other candidates. I like her. Do I write it?

A local paper asked me to write an op-ed about a zoning change that would raise my home's value. I genuinely think the change is good policy, but I would profit. Do I disclose it, decline, or write it anyway?

My apartment building's management installed a smart lock system that logs every fob entry and shares it with a private security contractor. I signed the lease before this. Tenants want me to organize a complaint. Do I, and how?

A city department asked me to design a survey about a new bike lane and to only include residents who own cars, because 'they are the ones affected.' I bike to work. Do I follow the request, widen the survey, or raise it with my supervisor?

Our HOA's pool gate now reads faces instead of key fobs, and the vendor keeps the images for 'safety review.' I'm the treasurer. A family says their teenager gets flagged because of a hoodie. I can cancel the contract or ask for a fix. What's right?
A local candidate's text bank is sending me scripts that include a claim about my opponent I believe is misleading. I get paid per shift. Do I keep texting, or quit and lose the income?

I sit on our town's library board, and a company offered free e-book kiosks if we let them place ads for a payday lender on the login screen. The library budget gap is real. Do I vote to accept the kiosks?

I volunteer at a food bank and the new intake app requires a photo ID scan for every household. Some people are undocumented and are turning away. My supervisor says it is a grant requirement. Do I follow the rule, quietly skip the scan, or raise it with the board?

The city's recycling app gave me a 'recycling champion' badge for reporting neighbors' bins. I got the badge by marking bins that turned out to be on a different collection schedule. Should I say something?
The county wants to use an algorithm to prioritize road repairs, and the vendor won't explain how it weighs poor neighborhoods. I am a public works analyst. Do I sign off on the report?

I am a poll worker and a voter asked me to help fill in their ballot because their eyesight is poor. The rules say I can assist only with a form and a second worker present, and the line is long. Do I help informally, follow the rule, or ask them to come back?

Our town's Facebook page is selling 'verified' blue-check status for local businesses through a third-party service, and I'm the page admin. It's not illegal, but it's misleading. Do I shut it down or keep the revenue?

A neighbor is running for school board and asked me to forward a mass email to parents I know. The email contains a claim about a teacher that I believe is exaggerated. I have the parent list from my PTA role. Should I forward it, edit out the claim, or decline?
I sit on a city board that meets over video, and a member keeps joining from a car during votes. The minutes record him as present. Do I raise the attendance question or let it go?
The city's website says a park is open until 10 p.m., but the gate now locks at dusk and people have been ticketed. I'm on the parks advisory group. Do I raise it publicly or quietly?

My town's emergency alert system has my number, and I got a test alert at 2 a.m. The settings let me opt out of non-weather alerts, but then I'd miss boil-water notices. I work early shifts. How should I set it?
A mutual-aid spreadsheet lists families who need rent help, with their addresses and kids' schools. I help maintain it. A journalist asked for access. Do I grant read-only or refuse?

The city's snowplow tracker app shows my street as plowed, but it hasn't been touched in two days. I can report the error in the app, which flags the driver, or post the truth in the neighborhood group. What should I do?

A city councilmember's staffer emailed me, a local reporter, offering an exclusive on a housing audit if I agree not to ask about the mayor's budget ties. I need the story. I also don't want to be used. How should I respond?

I sit on the county's redistricting advisory panel. The mapping software a consultant gave us has a 'community similarity' score built from shopping data, and it quietly groups my area with a wealthier one. I can flag it in the meeting or offline. Which?
The city's new 911 texting service auto-translates, and I saw a test where a Spanish message about a fire got mistranslated as 'no fire.' I work for the vendor. Do I report it before launch?
The city's bike-share app charges a deposit that hits low-income riders hardest, and I work for the vendor. I could push an internal change or leak the pricing memo to a reporter. What should I do?

The county's court reminder texts come from a number that looks like spam, and many people miss their dates. I know because I got a summons I almost ignored. Do I warn people with a mass text of my own?

I work at the DMV and our new kiosk camera uses facial recognition to verify identity. An elderly man's face does not match and he is getting upset; I can override with a supervisor code. My supervisor is at lunch. Should I override for him, make him wait, or tell him to come back?

The transit agency wants to replace paper passes with a phone app that tracks location 'to improve service.' I'm a bus driver and I know half my riders are unbanked. The agency is taking comments this week. Do I speak as a rider or as staff?
The city's compost program app asks me to photograph what I put in the bin for 'quality control.' My neighbor's kids sometimes add non-compostables. Do I submit photos that would get them fined?
My precinct needs a volunteer to drive ballots from polling places to the county office. I have a car and the time, but a friend says drivers are being doxxed online this cycle. Do I sign up?
My town is deciding whether to remove a statue from the square, and my ancestor donated the land it stands on. I have a chance to speak at the hearing. Should I say whose land it was?

The county health department's portal shows my vaccination record with an error in my birth year. Fixing it requires an in-person visit I cannot take off work for. Do I keep using the wrong record or push for a fix?
A friend running for school board asked me to moderate their Facebook group so critical comments get hidden as 'spam.' I agree with some of the criticism. Do I accept the role?
I am a volunteer EMT, and the dispatch app shows callers' addresses and medical notes. A friend's address popped up for a non-emergency, and I am tempted to check on them later. Should I?

The county fair now uses wristbands that track which stalls kids visit and sells the pattern to vendors. I'm the volunteer coordinator. A parent asked me if the bands are 'just for entry.' I don't fully know. What do I say?

The city's open-data portal accidentally published the home addresses of domestic-violence shelter residents in a spreadsheet. I downloaded it before they pulled it. Do I delete my copy or keep it as evidence?
A city council meeting moved online, and I can submit a comment under a screen name. I have strong views on a development. Do I use my real name or the handle?

My apartment building's management signed us all up for a package locker that photographs every delivery and every person who opens it. There was a clause buried in the lease renewal I clicked through. I'm the tenant rep on the building council. How hard should I push to get it removed?

My city council rep is hosting a 'telephone town hall' where residents press 1 to speak. I know the queue is screened by staff who drop critics. I have a question about the shelter contract. Do I call in and risk being cut, or show up in person?
I coach a youth league that uses an app to schedule games and collect fees. The app shows which families have not paid. I can see who is behind. Do I mention it privately or let the system handle it?
I'm on the planning commission and a developer who donated to my campaign has a project up for approval. I can recuse, which delays it, or vote and disclose. What should I do?

Our block association got a grant to plant trees, and the city's app lets us choose locations. The shadiest spots are in front of homes whose owners did not ask. Do I plant where it helps most or only where invited?

A local news site asked me, as a city clerk, to confirm a leaked draft of a contract before it publishes. The draft is real but not final, and confirming it could hurt the city's negotiating position. I am not supposed to talk to press. What should I do?
I'm a municipal clerk, and a councilmember asked me to backdate a permit approval by one day so it beats a neighbor's appeal deadline. The permit is for a shed that's actually fine. Should I do it?
The city's new eviction diversion program requires landlords to attend a mediation, and my tenant is behind on rent for the first time. I could skip mediation and file directly. Should I?
Our community garden's signup app has a waiting list, and I know the coordinator. A plot just opened and I could ask to be moved up. Another family has been waiting longer. What should I do?
A disaster-relief signup form asks for my disability status to prioritize aid. I do not have a disability, but my application would move faster if I checked the box. Do I?

I run a small community garden on city land. The parks department wants to pave half of it for a parking lot for a new rec center. They offered us a smaller plot across the highway. How should I respond?

I volunteer at the animal shelter, and the county wants to move to a kill-free contract only if we stop taking owner surrenders. I know several families who would just abandon pets instead. How should I weigh in at the hearing?

I coach a youth soccer league that gets free field time from the city in exchange for a banner crediting a councilmember. The banner now shows her campaign logo. Parents are asking me why. What should I do?
I sit on a citizens' advisory board for the police. The chief asked us to endorse a new drone program before the public comment period opens. I have questions about privacy. How should I respond?

I am a substitute teacher and the district's app flags me as 'unreliable' because I declined three shifts in a row while my mother was in the hospital. Now I get fewer offers. I can appeal but it takes weeks. Should I appeal, take worse shifts, or look for another district?

A local candidate's canvassing app shows me which houses have not voted in past elections and asks me to skip them. My own house is on the skip list. I am being paid to knock doors. Do I follow the list or knock every door?

I'm on a county broadband committee, and the provider we're about to fund wants to install equipment on church steeples with a clause letting it share 'anonymized' browsing data with advertisers. The church trustees asked my opinion. What should I tell them?
The DMV's online renewal let me pick 'prefer not to say' for a question I think is mandatory. I submitted it and got approved anyway. Do I go back and fix it?

I am a crossing guard and the school's app now tracks my location during shifts to confirm I am at my post. I take a bathroom break at the gas station across the street. Do I report the tracking or just adjust my route?

I volunteer at a legal aid clinic and a client's case file was left open on a shared laptop. I could close it and say nothing, or report it and risk the volunteer coordinator getting in trouble. What should I do?

A developer wants to put a 'smart mailbox' hub on our corner that photographs every package and logs who collects it, in exchange for free mailboxes for the block. I'm the block association chair. Some love it, some are worried. How should I guide the decision?

I sit on the library board, and a vendor pitched an AI book-recommendation tool that would replace our staff picks. It is cheaper, and our budget is tight, but the staff picks are why kids come. How should I vote?

I run the local food bank's volunteer schedule, and a city grant requires us to log immigration status of recipients for 'reporting.' Families are already scared. I could record 'declined' for everyone. What should I do?
Our food pantry got a surplus of expired baby formula. A volunteer wants to hand it out anyway because families are desperate. I'm the shift lead. What should I do?

A city council candidate asked me to run their social media, and part of the job is posting AI-generated images of the opponent looking tired or angry. The images are labeled 'satire' in tiny text. I need the paycheck. Should I take the job, refuse that part, or walk away?

A city council member asked me to sign a nondisclosure agreement about a development deal before I attend a public meeting. I am a volunteer planning commissioner. The meeting is supposed to be open. Do I sign, refuse, or attend without signing?

Our community center got a donation from a local casino to fund after-school programs, and some parents object on moral grounds. I manage the center and the programs would close without it. How should I decide?
The city offered me a rebate for a heat pump if I let them post my address on a public map of 'climate leaders.' My ex knows that address. Do I take the rebate or protect my privacy?

I'm on the board of our public-access TV station, and a resident submitted a show claiming the water is poisoned by a conspiracy. We air it or not under our rules. I think it's false but I can't prove it. How should I vote?

I drive a rideshare and a city survey offered me a gift card to report my wait times at the airport. The survey is anonymous, but if I report the truth, the airport may cut rideshare pickup spots, hurting my own income. Do I report honestly?
Our HOA board voted to hire an immigration-status check for renters. I'm the secretary and must send the letters. I think it's discriminatory, but I'm not sure it's illegal here. What should I do?

A parent in my daughter's class started an online petition to remove a book from the school library. I disagree with the petition but the parent is my carpool partner. The library is taking comments. Do I sign a counter-petition, speak at the meeting, or stay out of it?

Our HOA board wants me, as secretary, to record the annual meeting and post the video for absent owners. One owner is in the middle of a foreclosure and will say things she may regret. Do I post the full recording?

The county health department is doing wastewater tracking by neighborhood, and results get posted by block. My block has the highest readings and my landlord is already asking about it. Do I raise privacy concerns publicly?

The city hired me as a seasonal data-entry clerk for its rental-assistance program. I noticed the spreadsheet shows some families got denied because of a date-format error. My supervisor says fixing it is above my pay grade. What should I do?
The city replaced its comment hotline with a chatbot that answers in three languages but not the one most of my block speaks. I could volunteer to translate complaints informally. Is that my place?
My building's fire inspection report is available online, and it lists violations I know the landlord fixed but never re-filed. A tenant is asking me whether it is safe. What do I tell them?
The city's recycling app says my address is ineligible for curbside pickup because of a boundary line. I know the line is wrong from the map, but I could just use my neighbor's bin. What should I do?

The city's permit portal auto-rejects applications that do not fit a template, and I am the clerk who reviews appeals. A small contractor's application got rejected three times for formatting. I can push it through manually or tell him to resubmit. He is losing money. What should I do?

I'm a poll greeter and a campaign gave me a tablet that scans voters' faces to confirm they haven't already voted, using a party database. It's not the official check-in. I can keep using it or tell the county clerk. What's the right call?
The parks department wants to remove a mature oak for a new pickleball court, and my kids climb that tree. There is a public hearing and I could organize neighbors. How far should I take this?

The city's 911 system added a text option that routes through a vendor cloud, and I dispatch. During last month's storm, texts queued for twenty minutes while calls went through. I reported it and was told to 'log it as a glitch.' Do I push harder or go around my supervisor?

I run a small business and the city's new 'Shop Local' app features my store, but a competitor's listing was removed after I reported a minor address error. They think I did it on purpose. Should I tell them I did report the error, or stay quiet?

My city's 311 app lets residents attach photos to pothole reports. My neighbor keeps submitting photos of the same repaired pothole to make our block look neglected before a street-funding vote. I work part-time for the parks district. Should I flag the duplicate reports or stay out of it?

Our town's recycling app says glass is accepted, but I learned from a hauler that it goes to landfill. I could post the truth and tank participation, or stay quiet and let people feel good. What should I do?

Our school's parent portal now shows other families' lunch-debt balances on a shared dashboard by mistake. I can see names and amounts. The principal has not noticed. Do I tell her or keep quiet and hope IT fixes it?
Our town's holiday parade permit lottery is run on a spreadsheet a friend maintains. She offered to bump my scout troop up the list because we were late. Do I accept?

Our precinct needs poll workers, and the clerk asked me to recruit. I have a friend who is passionate but has posted angrily about one party. Training is short and the pay is small. Do I recommend them or not?

The city's new sidewalk-repair app ranks requests by how many neighbors upvote. My street is mostly renters who work nights; the richer street over has a block captain who organizes votes. Do I organize my block to compete?

I coach a youth soccer league, and the city's field-booking site now uses dynamic pricing that triples rates for working-class teams' usual slots. I can quietly pay more, or raise it at the parks board meeting. My parents can't afford more. What should I do?

I'm on the library board. A parent asked us to move a graphic novel to the adult section. I've read it; it's fine for teens. The vote is close and my neighbor is the parent. How should I handle my position?
The city is installing speed cameras near a school, and I got a ticket in the mail for a time I know I was at work. I could contest it, but the camera has reduced speeding. What should I do?
The water utility's app lets me see usage by address, and I noticed my neighbor's meter shows a leak running for weeks. I have their number from a block party. Do I call them or the utility first?
I am on a citizen review board for police complaints, and a case involves an officer who coached my son's soccer team. I could recuse or stay and argue for a fair outcome. Which is right?

I am a city bus driver and the new scheduling app auto-assigns me shifts with a two-minute gap between routes. It is physically impossible to make the connection, so the app marks me late. My supervisor says to 'just log the delays.' Should I log them honestly, ask for a change, or stop worrying about the metric?

I'm the admin for our neighborhood association's new portal, and a board member asked me to delete the comment thread where residents questioned the landscaping contract awarded to his brother-in-law. The comments are still visible in my backup. He says it's 'routine cleanup.' What should I do?
I volunteered to moderate my town's online forum. A post names a local business as a front for something illegal, citing no source. It might be true. Do I take it down?

Our neighborhood's emergency alert group is run on a platform that requires a phone number and shares it with 'partners.' I'm the admin. An older resident without a smartphone asked to be added through her landline, and the system won't. How do I handle her request?

I'm on the library board and a vendor pitched an AI that reads scanned local newspapers to answer genealogy questions, but it would send the scans to a server overseas. The archive includes obituaries of living families. The vote is next month. How should I lean?

Our municipal broadband project is over budget, and the consultant's report I was asked to endorse was partly written by the vendor bidding on the contract. I sit on the oversight committee. How should I proceed?

I'm the treasurer of a small volunteer fire department, and the new online donation platform takes a 5% cut by default. We can switch to a cheaper option, but the current one has been shared widely and switching means losing donors. What should I do?

Our library's app lets me place holds, and I noticed a neighbor's account is still checked out on a book I returned. I work at the front desk part-time. Fixing it means opening their record without a request. What should I do?

The county's vaccine appointment site has a hidden URL that lets people skip the queue, and I found it because I used to work in IT there. My elderly neighbor cannot get a slot. Do I share the link with her?

I'm a crossing guard, and a parent asked me to let their kid cross a half-block early so they can make their shift. Doing it once sets a precedent I can't manage. Refusing means a stressed parent is late. What should I do?
I'm a notary, and a neighbor asked me to notarize a signature on an absentee-ballot envelope for a relative who isn't present. The signature looks real and the voter is elderly. Should I refuse?

Our HOA's online portal now requires me to upload a photo of my car's license plate to get a guest parking pass for my mother's weekly dialysis ride. The pass is only valid for her visits, but the system stores the plate and links it to my address permanently. I can refuse and pay the visitor lot each week. What should I do?
A nonprofit asked me to canvass for a ballot measure funding mental health services, and I know the measure also cuts a program my cousin relies on. Do I knock on doors for it?

A local news site asked me to be a 'community fact-checker' on a rumor about a school budget cut. The editor wants my real name and photo, and the rumor started with someone I know. I can confirm it is false. Should I go on the record?
I sit on a nonprofit board that receives city grants. The mayor's office hinted our grant renewal depends on us endorsing his housing plan at a hearing. Do I speak in favor?

The city's affordable-housing lottery portal let me see a list of applicants because of a permissions bug. My own cousin is on it. I could quietly check the odds or report the bug and delay the draw. What should I do?
The county's property tax portal shows my assessment and my neighbor's side by side. Mine is lower for a similar house. Do I point out the error that favors me?

Our water district sent a text alert about a boil-water notice, but the link goes to a site that asks for my Social Security number to 'confirm service.' I am almost sure it is a scam. Do I ignore it, warn neighbors, or report it and risk spreading panic?

I moderate a community subreddit for our city, and a local council candidate keeps posting technically-true-but-misleading claims that skirt our rules. Removing them looks partisan; leaving them amplifies them. What should I do?
My block's WhatsApp group is planning to report a nearby encampment through the city's app. I think some of those reports will lead to sweeps. Do I stay in the group or speak up?
A city council candidate asked to put a yard sign in my lawn, and my homeowner association bans political signs. I agree with the candidate. Do I put it up and risk the fine?
A candidate knocked on my door and asked to put a sign in my yard. I support her opponent but don't want to be rude. She's also my kid's dentist. What do I say?
I'm a volunteer EMT. On a call, I saw a city councilmember's adult son clearly impaired and driving. He wasn't the patient. Reporting it would mean my name in a small town. What should I do?

I run a neighborhood tool-lending library. A contractor borrowed our generator and has not returned it; I know he is behind on bills. Chasing him publicly in the group chat would shame him. What is fair?
The city's pothole app marked my report 'resolved' without any repair. I can reopen it, but the crew lead is a friend of my dad. Do I escalate to the council or let it go?

The library's holds system shows me that a book on a controversial topic has forty requests, many from one account. I volunteer at the front desk and could flag the account to staff. Should I say something or let the request list stand?

The city's benefits portal asked applicants to upload a selfie to 'verify identity,' and I've heard elderly applicants failing because the software can't match old photos. I volunteer at the senior center helping people apply. Do I keep helping them fail, or stop and report?

A school fundraiser is using a cash-back app that tracks purchases and donates a percentage. Signing up means sharing my spending with a vendor. My kid wants the class to win a pizza party. Do I join?

Our mutual-aid group got a donation from a local business owner who is running for office and now wants to speak at every distribution. Some members are uncomfortable. I handle the schedule. What should I do?

Our public defender's office is using an AI tool to draft bail arguments, and I'm a paralegal. A draft it produced misstated a client's address to a judge, who read it aloud. I caught it after the hearing. Do I report it up, or help the client quietly?

The city's noise-complaint line now uses an automated voice that routes calls by zip code. I know the wealthier zip gets a human. My complaint about a late-night site is real. Do I use a friend's address to get through?

My city installed license plate readers at the park entrance, and the police say they only keep data 30 days, but the contract says 90. I found this through a records request I filed as a resident. Do I publish it?
A local news tip line asked for my photos of a flooded intersection. I took them from my porch. If I send them, my address could be identified by the angle. Do I send them anyway?

I volunteer translating at a city housing workshop. A family told me privately they are undocumented and asked me not to put their names on the sign-in sheet. The city requires the sheet. What do I do?

I sit on a citizens' oversight board for the police, and I received an anonymous letter alleging misconduct by an officer whose brother coaches my kid's team. I can't verify the letter. How do I handle it?

I'm a census-style volunteer for a local needs survey, and the tablet I carry records GPS even when I'm not entering data. The nonprofit running it says it's for mapping gaps. Some households want me to skip their door. How do I proceed?
A local nonprofit asked me to translate their ballot guide into my language for free. The deadline is tight and I have a paid translation job the same week. Do I take it on?

I volunteer at the library's computer help desk. An older man asked me to log into his benefits portal and change his address for him, which I can do with his password. Doing it for him is against the rules, but he genuinely cannot see the screen. What should I do?

I'm on the neighborhood watch group chat, and someone posted a Ring video of a 'suspicious' person who I recognize as the new aide at the group home. He was just waiting for a client. Do I correct the post publicly?

The school district's parent portal shows my son's test scores before they're officially released. A friend who teaches there asked me not to share them. Another parent is asking me for the numbers. What do I say?
I volunteer at a shelter that uses facial recognition at the door for 'safety.' A guest asked me if they are being scanned. I know they are. Do I tell the truth or defer to staff?

Our HOA's online voting portal shows how each household voted on a dues increase. I voted no because I cannot afford it, and now a neighbor is asking why I 'voted against the pool.' The portal was supposed to be secret. Do I confront the board, explain myself, or stay quiet?
The city's new 911 app lets me report noise complaints anonymously, but my neighbor's teenager's band plays until midnight. I could report them or talk to them. What should I do?

Our voting precinct moved to a church basement, and the church's Wi-Fi now runs the check-in laptops. I'm the site lead. The church asked to see the roster 'for its own records.' I said no, but the county told them it was fine. What do I do now?

I'm a bus driver, and the new scheduling algorithm keeps assigning me splits that leave two unpaid hours midday, which I can't afford. My union rep says file a grievance; my supervisor says the algorithm can't be changed. What should I do?

The county's mental-health crisis line now routes calls through a chatbot that decides who gets a human. I answer the phones. Last week a caller in crisis got stuck in the bot and hung up. I can escalate this internally or tell a reporter. What's the right move?
A local mosque asked to use the community center for Friday prayers, and a few residents complained about parking. I manage the center's bookings. Do I grant the request as I would any other group?
A city council member offered me a paid advisory role right after I testified against their housing plan. Taking it would give me influence; refusing keeps my criticism credible. What should I do?
The recycling app gives points for scanning items, and I noticed I can scan the same bottle repeatedly. My kids are competitive about the leaderboard. Do I tell them to stop?
A councilmember's office emailed me a draft zoning map before the public meeting because I once donated. I could share it with my neighbors who oppose the change. Do I?

A city survey asks residents to rank which parks get upgrades, and I can submit multiple times by clearing my browser. My park is losing by a handful of votes. Do I stuff the ballot for my kids' playground?

My town's emergency alert system sent a false evacuation warning during a storm drill, and I was the one who saw the test flag before it went out. I could post on the neighborhood app that it was a mistake, but the county says only official channels should confirm. People are panicking. What should I do?
My city launched a text line to report abandoned cars. I used it, and a week later the same car's owner, a coworker, asked if I knew who reported him. I do. What should I say?
My town's new online permitting system rejected my neighbor's fence application without explanation, and I work in the clerk's office. I could look up the reason for them. Is that appropriate?
A local candidate's text-banking tool keeps messaging my number even after I opted out. I know the volunteer running it from church. Do I report the campaign to the state or just text him personally?

I volunteer as a poll greeter, and a candidate's app is paying people per signup we scan at the door. The money would cover my bus fare and then some. I think it quietly turns a civic favor into a paid side hustle. Should I keep scanning?

I volunteer at a free clinic that uses a donated scheduling tool from a vendor who also lobbies against the clinic's funding. Leaving the tool would drop patients; staying supports the vendor. What should I do?
My HOA's online voting portal lets me see how many units have voted but not who. I own two units through a family trust and could cast both. The rules are unclear on whether that's allowed. Should I?
I am on the jury pool for a case involving a local business owner I recognize from my gym. I can probably stay fair, but I could also mention it and be excused. What should I say during questioning?

The local food bank switched to an app where I reserve a pickup slot. I noticed slots for seniors open an hour early, and I qualify only if I check a box I am not sure applies to me. Should I check it to feed my family?
I'm a poll worker. A voter's registration shows an old address, and the person insists they updated it online. I can offer a provisional ballot or send them to another site. What should I do?

The hospital's patient portal now sends appointment reminders through a chatbot that also upsells screenings, and my mom clicked through to a paid test she didn't need. I work in the billing office. Do I report the vendor, or just cancel the charge for her?
I'm a volunteer at a cooling center during a heat wave. The church hosting us wants to hand out religious pamphlets with the water. Some guests have complained. I'm coordinating. What should I do?

Our town's new 311 app lets residents report 'suspicious loitering' with a photo, and the reports feed a heat map police use to schedule patrols. I noticed my own block is lighting up because teens wait there for the bus. I use the app. Should I file a correction, or is that misusing a channel meant for emergencies?

I volunteer at a food pantry that now requires an app to log each household's visits. A woman asked me to log her under her sister's ID so her immigration status won't be in the system. I believe her fear is real. What should I do?

Our mutual-aid group got a grant that requires us to log every person we help in a shared spreadsheet, names and addresses included, so the city can 'measure impact.' People we serve are undocumented. I keep the sheet. How do I handle this?
Our tenant association voted to withhold rent over a broken elevator. I'm the treasurer and I think the landlord will evict the most vulnerable family first. Do I collect the money anyway?

The city's permit portal auto-approves small solar installations if the address is in a certain zone, and my address qualifies, but I know the zone was drawn before my street was rezoned for fire risk. Should I take the fast approval or file the full review?

I sit on the school board, and the district's new bus-routing software sends parents a live map of the bus, which also reveals where kids with special-needs stops get on. A parent flagged it. The vendor says it's a feature. How should I vote on keeping it?

Our apartment building's package room has a camera feed the landlord shares with a private security app. I can see my neighbors' deliveries and comings and goings. Do I ask to be removed or warn the tenants?
