The city's parking app charged me twice and a refund requires a paper form at an office that's only open Tuesday mornings. My councilmember's aide offered to 'push it through' if I attend a town hall. Should I?
The library is hosting a drag story hour, and a group asked me, as a trustee, to cancel it for 'safety.' I have kids who attend. What should I do?
The county fair board wants to book a rodeo that uses calf roping, and animal welfare groups are organizing. I am on the board and my family has ranched here for generations. How should I vote?

The city installed a sidewalk sensor that counts pedestrians and, I found out, detects phones to estimate crowd size. It's in front of my store. The data goes to a retail analytics firm. I'm on the merchants' association. Do I demand removal or ask for a cut?

I'm a translator volunteering at a naturalization clinic. One applicant told me in confidence that a document he submitted has a wrong date. If I report it, he may be denied. If I don't, I'd be helping a false statement. What should I do?

Our community center's free legal clinic now requires clients to consent to having their conversations recorded by an AI notetaker 'for quality.' I'm the volunteer coordinator. A client in a custody case asked me if it's private. I don't know. What do I tell her?

A council member asked me, as a precinct captain, to hand over the list of people who requested mail ballots so their campaign can 'remind' them. The list is public but this feels different. What do I do?
A local news site asked me, as a witness to a fire, to share my phone video. It shows a neighbor's kids and their address. The fire was real and the story matters. Do I share it?
A statewide petition to expand ranked-choice voting is circulating, and the signature gatherers are paid per signature. I support the idea but saw one gatherer mislead a voter. Do I sign anyway?

Our neighborhood association wants to use a facial-recognition doorbell to screen visitors at the community center. I run the front desk and would have to explain it to people. Do I object or go along?
I'm a census outreach volunteer. A family asked me to fill out their form for them because they don't read English well. I can, but I'm supposed to only assist. What should I do?

Our public school's lunch app scans kids' faces to speed the line and charges the account without a PIN. My son is on free lunch and kids noticed the separate tray. I'm a parent volunteer. Should I ask the principal to change it or go to the board?

A city chatbot told me my permit application was approved, but the portal still shows it pending. I could print the chat transcript and start work, or wait. The contractor is charging me for idle days. What should I do?

I run the scoreboard for a city rec league and the new app auto-posts scores to a betting site. Parents are asking me to turn it off but the league says the sponsorship pays for the field lights. I control the app login. What should I do?

The county health department's appointment app keeps giving my elderly neighbor slots in a distant clinic because of a glitch with her address. I figured out a workaround by typing a nearby ZIP. Is it okay to use the workaround, or should I report the bug and let her miss this round?

Our transit agency's app now asks riders to rate drivers, and a driver I know is being dinged by one repeat complainer. I can leave a five-star review to offset it, though I have not ridden with him recently. Should I?

The park district's new app lets people reserve picnic tables, and a reseller is grabbing all the summer weekends to flip them. I'm a parks aide. Families keep asking me to fix it at the window. Do I tell them how it works or stay quiet?

The city's online portal for utility assistance asked for my immigration status to 'verify eligibility.' A neighbor told me the field is optional but the form will not submit without it. I need the help this month. Do I fill it in, call the office, or wait?
The school district is surveying parents about a later start time, and my employer's shift means I can't make either option work. I can answer honestly and skew the result toward 'no.' Should I?

I volunteer registering voters at a farmers market. A man in a campaign shirt is handing out water nearby, which is legal, but he is also telling people where to stand. Do I say something or let it go?

My city's open-data portal published a dataset of code complaints that includes my name and address from a complaint I filed about a slumlord. Now it is searchable. I can ask them to remove my name, but that might delay the fix. What should I do?

I am a volunteer election observer, and I saw a poll worker quietly turn away a voter over an ID issue I think was wrong. Reporting it delays the count; not reporting it lets it pass. What should I do?
A city employee leaked me a draft plan to close the only bus route that serves the night shift at the hospital. I am a reporter's neighbor and could tip them off before the vote. Should I?
The voter registration drive I help with uses a paper form that asks for a phone number I know is optional. A volunteer is marking it required. Do I correct her in front of the line or after?

My polling place moved to a church basement two miles further and the notice only went out on the county website. I have a car and several elderly neighbors do not. Do I offer rides on election day, or is that overstepping?

I'm a crossing guard, and the school district swapped our radios for an app that shares our location with parents during shifts. A parent used it to track me to my car. I can ask to go back to radios or just keep using it. What should I do?

I volunteer as a poll greeter, and a voter asked me to help her fill in the bubble for a school board race because her English is limited. Helping is technically electioneering. Refusing feels cruel. What should I do?
A former coworker asked me to be a reference, but I remember they left out that they were asked to leave. The new employer's form asks if they're eligible for rehire. What do I write?

My ex keeps texting me late at night 'just to check in' and I keep answering because I do not want to be cold. My current partner has said it makes her uncomfortable. I told her it is nothing. Do I block him or keep explaining?
My neighbor asked me to watch her kids 'for twenty minutes' three times this week, and each time it's been over two hours. I have my own work deadlines. How do I set a boundary kindly?
My roommate's alarm keeps going off through a smart speaker I also control. I can mute it from my phone, but they've asked me never to touch their settings. Do I mute it tonight anyway?
My landlord's son, who's my age, messaged me on a social app asking me out. My lease is up for renewal in two months. Do I tell him I'm not interested and risk the renewal, or just go quiet?

My dad keeps forwarding me health articles from a group chat and asking if he should stop his blood pressure pills. I'm not a doctor, but I did take one biology class. How do I answer without becoming his pharmacist?

A close friend is planning to move in with a partner she's known for two months, and she wants me to co-sign the lease as a 'character reference.' I think it's a mistake. Do I say yes, say why not, or say nothing?
My partner and I share a calendar app, and I noticed they've been adding 'work dinners' that overlap with plans we made. I haven't asked who they're with. Do I check or ask directly?
My roommate asked me to pretend I don't know she's been seeing her ex again, because her family would be upset. Her ex is also my friend and has been asking me to vouch for him. What should I do?
My coworker and I both applied for the same internal promotion, and she asked me to practice interview questions with her. I want the job too. Do I help her prepare honestly or hold back?

A group chat of college friends is planning a surprise party for someone who told me privately she's overwhelmed and doesn't want a fuss this year. If I say something I break her confidence. What should I do?

My roommate's freelance client keeps texting me because her phone died and she listed me as backup contact on an invoice. The client is frantic about a deadline she never told me about. Do I pass along the messages I can see on our shared tablet, or stay out of it?
My mother keeps calling my workplace to check on me, and my manager has noticed. I love her but it's embarrassing. Do I set a firm boundary or ask my manager to screen calls?
My in-laws want to stay at our place for a month during the holidays, and my partner already said yes without asking me. I have a demanding job and need quiet. How do we handle this?
A friend asked me to review a contract they're about to sign through a freelance app, and I spotted a clause that lets the client use their work forever. They're excited to start. Do I raise it?

My close friend's partner is controlling and has isolated her from us, and she just invited me to lunch and asked me to keep it between us. I want to stay in her life without pushing her away. How do I handle lunch?
My boss asked me to cover for him by saying he was in a client meeting when he was actually at his kid's soccer game. I have to answer honestly if the client asks. What do I do?
My coworker friend asked me to cover for her so she could leave early for a date, and I'd have to lie to our boss about where she was. She's done favors for me before. Do I agree?

My roommate never cleans the bathroom and claims she does 'her share' when I'm not looking. I've started keeping score, which feels awful. Do I make a chore chart and risk the tension, or keep quietly cleaning?
A friend asked me to review her resume and I noticed she lists a degree she never finished. She's applying at a company where I know the hiring manager. Do I tell her, or tell him, or neither?

My girlfriend wants me to meet her parents, but her dad has made comments I've heard secondhand that I find pretty offensive. She says he'll warm up to me. Do I go and bite my tongue, or say something now?

My sister asked me to be her emergency contact on a sobriety app that pings me when she checks into a bar. She relapsed last week and I saw it before her sponsor did. Do I tell her sponsor or wait for her to bring it up?
I'm in a wedding party group chat where the couple is fighting about money through the planner. The bride privately asked me to talk the groom down. Do I get in the middle?

My old friend from high school keeps reaching out to 'catch up,' and I suspect she wants to sell me something. I don't want to be rude, but I also don't want the pitch. Do I meet her, or politely decline?
My coworker told me in confidence she's pregnant and hasn't told our manager, who is planning to put her on a demanding project. I'm her teammate. Do I protect her secret or the team?
A friend keeps asking me to review her writing and then argues with every note. I'm exhausted and want to be honest. How do I tell her I can't keep doing this?

My wife's brother is getting married and asked me to give a toast, then hinted he wants me to leave out the divorce and the estrangement from their father. The honest version is complicated. What do I write?

My grandfather's caregiver sends me updates I didn't ask for, including photos of him in private moments. My aunt, who hired her, says it's fine. Do I tell the caregiver to stop or go over my aunt's head?
A friend asked me to co-host her baby shower and to exclude another friend she's feuding with. The excluded friend will find out and be hurt. Do I agree to the exclusion?

My roommate's boyfriend stays over five nights a week and uses our utilities, but she insists he's 'not living here' on the lease. I split rent with her. How do I raise this without blowing up the friendship?
A friend is planning to post a 'before and after' of her weight loss and tagged me in the before photo without asking. I didn't consent to that being public. Do I ask her to untag me or let it go?

My partner's best friend is rude to me every time we're together, and my partner says I should give him another chance. I'm tired of being the bigger person. Do I insist on boundaries, or keep tolerating it for my partner's sake?
My partner and I are splitting up and she wants to keep the dog. I'm the one who walks him and pays the vet. She says she'll be lonely without him. How do we decide without this turning ugly?
A neighbor I barely know asked to use my Wi-Fi for a few weeks while hers is set up. I worry about what gets traced to my account. How do I decline without offending her?
My brother asked me to lend him my truck to move, and I know he'll drive it back with an empty tank and a scratch. He's family and he's had a rough year. Do I say yes or make an excuse?

My landlord is a nice older man who's been renting to me below market for years. He just raised the rent and I found out he's charging the new tenant upstairs less. Do I bring it up or count my blessings?

An old friend from high school, who I have not spoken to in years, messaged me asking for money for a medical bill and sent a photo of a hospital form. I cannot verify it and I remember she had a history of scams. Do I send something to be safe or ask for proof?
My partner's mother comments on my weight every time we visit, and my partner says that's just how she is and I should ignore it. I'm starting to dread family dinners. What do I say, and to whom?
My friend group's shared budget app shows one person has been covering more than their share for months but saying nothing. I only know because I have admin access. Do I bring it up with the group?
A friend asked me to proofread her novel, and it's not very good. She's asking if it's ready to send to agents. Do I tell her it needs work, and if so, how honest do I get?

My partner's calendar is shared with me for logistics, and I saw a recurring block labeled 'therapy' that they never mentioned. It explains a lot but I only know because of the calendar. Do I say something?

A friend asked me to babysit her kids during an emergency, but I have a work deadline that night and no backup. Do I cancel my work plans to help her, or tell her I can't and risk her not having anyone else?
My partner and I are splitting costs, and I found out they've been paying less than we agreed while telling me they paid in full. Do I confront them or quietly rebalance?

My cousin asked to stay with us 'for a few weeks' after a breakup, and it's now been three months. My partner is fed up. Do I give him a deadline and risk the family drama, or keep waiting for him to leave on his own?
A friend keeps canceling plans last minute and then posting about other outings on social media. She's going through a divorce, and I want to be patient. How do I set a limit without abandoning her?
I overheard through a shared gaming headset that a friend's partner is planning to propose, and my friend has told me they want to be the one to propose. Do I warn my friend?
My landlord is also my friend and asked me to vouch for him to a new tenant who's worried about the building's maintenance history. I know the elevator has been broken for months. What do I say?
My sister wants me to keep a secret from our parents that she's dropping out of college, and they're paying the tuition. Do I keep her confidence, or tell them before they waste more money?
An old friend asked me to write a glowing recommendation for a program she's applying to, but I've seen her struggle and I'd be exaggerating. She'll see the letter. What do I write?

My best friend's fiancé added me on a fitness app, and I can see he logs runs at 6 a.m. at an address that isn't their apartment. She asked me last month to tell her if anything felt off. Do I say something?

A friend asked me to watch her dog for two weeks, and I said yes before realizing I'll be traveling for work part of that time. Do I back out now and disappoint her, or scramble to find a sitter and pay for it myself?
A friend asked me to be a reference for a job I know she'd struggle with, and the hiring manager is someone I respect. She's desperate for income. What do I tell each of them?

A coworker asked me to cover for her saying she was sick when she was actually at a job interview. She got the job and is leaving in two weeks. Our boss just asked me if she seemed off. What do I say?
My sibling and I share access to our dad's medical portal. I saw a note that his memory tests are getting worse, and my sibling keeps insisting he's fine to live alone. Do I forward the note?

My friend's mom is on a neighborhood app asking for a ride to a doctor's appointment, and my friend told me her mom isn't supposed to drive but is fine to be driven. I don't know her well. Do I offer or mind my business?
My neighbor borrowed my ladder and returned it broken with no apology, and I need it this weekend. Do I ask him to replace it, or eat the cost to avoid a feud?

A friend asked me to be a sperm donor for her and her wife. I want to help, but I'm worried about what it means for me in ten years. Do I say yes now and sort it out later, or be honest that I'm unsure?
My neighbor's teenager asked me to cover for him so he could go to a concert his mom forbade. He mows my lawn and I like him. She texted me asking if he was at my house. What do I say?
My ex keeps liking my posts from a fake account I figured out is theirs. We ended badly and I've asked for space. Do I block the fake account, call them out, or just ignore it?
My friend asked me to watch her kids for an hour and came back four hours later with no explanation. She asked me to do it again this weekend. Do I agree, ask what happened, or say no?
A close friend asked me to review their dating profile, and the bio contains a lie about their job that I know would bother people. Do I tell them it's dishonest, or just suggest small edits?
My neighbor's dog barks all day while she's at work, and she asked me to text her if it's a problem. I work from home and my calls keep getting interrupted. She's a single mom. What should I do?

My son's teacher messaged me privately that another parent is spreading a rumor about my kid bullying hers. I don't believe it, but the teacher asked me not to say who told me. How do I approach the other parent?

My dad's new wife manages his phone and has started answering my texts as him, saying he is 'resting.' I saw him last week and he seemed fine and asked why I had stopped calling. I do not know if she is protecting him or isolating him. How do I handle this?

My roommate's unemployment benefits letter came to our apartment and I can see she's been collecting while working under the table at her cousin's shop. She's behind on rent and I need her to pay. What do I do?

I promised my dying neighbor I would look after her cat, and now I am moving to a place that does not allow pets. My sister has offered to take the cat but keeps hinting she will rehome it. Do I keep my promise literally or find the cat the best home?

I found out through a shared calendar that my friend's surprise anniversary dinner is the same night as her husband's work trip, which he clearly forgot about. Do I tell her, tell him, or let it play out?

My coworker and I carpool, and she has started taking personal calls on speaker during the drive that include details about her marriage I never asked to know. If I ask her to stop, the ride gets awkward for an hour each way. What should I say?

A close friend announced her pregnancy and asked me, in front of a group, to be the godparent. I am not religious and I am not sure I want that lifelong role. Everyone was watching and I mumbled something. What do I say now?
A neighbor asked me to feed their cat while they're away and gave me their door code. While there, I saw mail from a collection agency piling up. Do I mention it, or leave it alone?
My neighbor keeps parking in my assigned spot and says the building never gave her one. I have the lease showing it's mine. She's otherwise lovely. How do I get my spot back without a feud?
Our group chat has a running joke about one guy's divorce that he laughs off every time. Last night he went quiet and left. Do I message him privately, or would that make it a thing?
My partner's sister asked me to keep a secret about her new relationship from my partner, who she says will 'freak out.' I don't like keeping things from my partner. Do I agree or push back?

My landlord added me to a building app where tenants rate each other on noise and tidiness. I can see a neighbor gave me a low rating because of my late shifts, which aren't against the rules. Do I respond in the app?

A close friend shares custody of her kids and posted a photo of her daughter's new school on a public account I follow. Her ex has been trying to find the school. Do I text her to take it down, knowing she'll feel judged, or just let it go?
A close friend lent me her car for a week and it got a small scratch in a parking lot. She hasn't noticed. I can afford to fix it quietly or tell her and risk awkwardness. What should I do?
My son's best friend's parents let the boys play violent games and stay up late, and my son now says I'm unfair. I don't want to judge them or alienate my son. How do I handle the difference?
I found out a close friend has been telling a mutual friend private things I told her about my health. She hasn't apologized and may not know I know. Do I confront her or quietly pull back?

My sister asked me to be her maid of honor, but she also invited my ex to the wedding and expects me to sit at the same table and give a toast. I haven't told her the breakup was ugly. Do I agree or say why I can't?
I found my roommate's journal open on the kitchen table with an entry about me. I only read a line before I realized what it was. Do I admit I saw it, or act like I didn't?

A coworker asked me to swap shifts so she can attend her daughter's recital, but I already have tickets to a concert that night. She rarely asks for favors. How do I say no without damaging the relationship?
I found out through a mutual friend's public post that someone I'm close to is moving away in a month. They haven't told me. Do I act surprised when they do, or ask them now?
A friend asked me to drive her to an appointment and wait, which will take my whole afternoon. I have a deadline. She has no one else. Do I rearrange my day or say no?

A group chat I have been in since college is planning a trip and voted to keep costs down by booking one room for four people. I have a medical condition that makes shared sleeping arrangements miserable. I can afford my own room but they will read it as me thinking I am above them. What do I do?
My dad's new wife asked me to call her 'Mom' in front of my younger siblings, who lost their mother two years ago. I don't want to hurt her, but it feels wrong. How do I handle it?

My mom asked me to manage her pharmacy auto-refills, and the app now shows every prescription she picks up. I noticed she stopped one that she told the family she still takes. Do I confront her or keep quiet?
My roommate and I split bills evenly, but he's been running the heat at 78 all winter and now the bill is double. He says he's cold and can't help it. Do I ask him to pay more, or eat it?

A friend's wedding registry is linked to a site that quietly adds a service fee, and guests in our group chat are complaining. I figured out the fee because I run a similar shop. Do I tell the couple or the guests?
I overheard two friends making plans for a trip and mentioning that they'd invite me 'if she weren't so flaky.' I am sometimes flaky. Do I confront them or just try to be better?
A friend is spreading a GoFundMe for her sick dog, and I suspect the money won't go where she says. I don't want to accuse her wrongly. Do I donate, ask questions, or stay quiet?

I'm in a wedding party and the group chat is planning a bachelorette that costs more than my rent. The bride is my oldest friend and I don't want to be the one who ruins it. Do I say I can't afford it or quietly drop out?

My partner wants to post about our relationship on social media constantly, and I prefer to keep us private. He says I'm hiding something. Do I compromise and post more, or hold my line and risk the fight?

I donated to a friend's medical fundraiser on a crowdfunding site, and now the site emails me other patients' campaigns with their diagnoses and photos. It feels like rubbernecking. Do I turn off the emails or say something to the site?

I donated blood, and the center now calls me every week to donate again and asks about my medications. I feel guilty saying no, but the calls are stressful. Do I block the number or explain why I am stopping?

My partner and I use a shared calendar app that synced my recurring 'infusion' appointments, and their family now sees them because of a shared group I forgot about. I was not ready to explain my treatment. Do I address it or quietly change the settings?

I wear a continuous glucose monitor and the manufacturer's app shares anonymized data with a research partner. The opt-out is buried and resets after each update. I want to keep using the alerts. How should I handle this?

I bought a smartwatch that detects irregular heartbeats and it flagged something. My doctor says it is probably noise but I cannot get an appointment for months. Do I go to the ER or trust the watch?

My team's shared drive auto-syncs to everyone's laptop, and I noticed a folder labeled 'reorg' that I was never meant to see. It shows my own role being merged away in six weeks. Should I tell anyone I saw it, or quietly start job hunting?
My gym's app posts my workouts to a leaderboard by default, and a coworker keeps commenting on my pace. I can go private, but the gym gives discounts for public streaks. What should I do?

My team's shared calendar auto-declines any meeting invite that overlaps my 'focus blocks,' but my manager keeps booking over them and telling me to just move the block. I set those blocks because I do school pickup. Do I keep moving them or push back?

My employer's expense app flagged my taxi receipt as suspicious because it was late at night near a bar. It was a legitimate ride home after a client dinner. Do I explain the details or resubmit quietly?

My apartment's online portal charged me a late fee because the payment page timed out during a storm. I have a screenshot of the error. Do I escalate publicly on the building's review page or just email management?

I found out through a shared Google Doc's version history that a colleague edited my performance feedback to remove a concern before it went to HR. The change favors me. Do I flag it, or let it stand since it helps me?

A friend asked me to be a reference on a rental application, and the landlord's portal asks me to confirm her income, which I know she inflated. I want her to get the place. Do I confirm it or decline to answer?

My company's chat tool shows when I am online, and my manager expects quick replies even on weekends. I have started appearing offline to get space. Is this dishonest enough that I should tell my manager?

I manage our team's shared drive and found a folder of salary spreadsheets that should be locked down. Fixing permissions could block a project that depends on them, and I'd be the one who changed it. Do I lock it or flag it?

My employer uses a time-tracking app that takes random screenshots of my screen. I sometimes check my kid's school portal during lunch. The app does not distinguish. Do I tell my manager or just stop?
A colleague asked me to endorse her on a professional network for a skill I know she doesn't have. She's a friend and job-hunting. Do I write a vague endorsement or decline?
A recruiter messaged me on a professional network offering a role that pays more but is a contract gig. My current job's pension vests in eight months. I keep the chat open. What should I do?

A job I applied to sent an automated rejection, then a human emailed asking me to interview anyway. The role pays less than my last one but I need work. Do I point out the contradiction or just say yes?
My workplace survey promised anonymity but asks for my department and tenure, which together identify me. My honest answers would criticize my manager. Do I answer fully or hedge?

I am a freelance designer, and a client I found through a marketplace wants to pay off-platform to avoid fees, which breaks the site's rules. They are my biggest account. Do I take the risk or lose them?

I'm applying for jobs and a former manager agreed to be a reference but asked me to write the reference letter myself for him to sign. The draft would be honest but flattering. Do I write it or ask him to do it himself?

I am selling furniture online, and a buyer sent a payment screenshot that looks edited. The platform says I should ship once the funds 'clear,' but the app still shows pending. Do I trust the screenshot and ship?

My side business's website got a takedown notice claiming my logo infringes a bigger company's. It looks like a stretch, but fighting it means legal fees I can't afford. Do I change the logo quietly or push back?
A former coworker's memorial page is collecting donations through a link I cannot verify. I want to give, but the organizer is someone I do not recognize. How do I proceed?

My team uses a shared AI writing tool, and I saw it suggested a sentence that quotes a customer's complaint nearly word for word in a public FAQ draft. Approving the draft means the customer could recognize themselves. Do I flag it and delay the launch?
My company's password manager flagged that a teammate reused a password from a breach. I can see the alert because I am the admin. Do I tell him privately or escalate to security?

My therapist's portal auto-sends appointment reminders to the email on file, which is my work address, and I just noticed my manager is on the same shared inbox alias. Do I confront the practice or hope nobody reads it?

My bank's app flagged a transfer from my sibling as possible fraud and froze my account. The only way to unfreeze it is to video-call a support agent and show my ID. I am traveling and my ID is at home. What now?

A former coworker keeps tagging me in LinkedIn posts about a scandal at my old employer, and people assume I agree because I don't untag. I left on good terms and still rely on that network. Should I ask her to stop or just quietly remove the tags?

I found a small local business's website is leaking customer card numbers, and I'm not a customer but I noticed while browsing. Reporting it means emailing a stranger who may not believe me. Do I bother?

The community pool's booking app now requires a deposit per slot, and if you cancel within an hour you lose it. My kid's swim lesson times keep shifting at work. Do I keep booking and risk the fees or stop going?
I applied for a loan online and the form asked for my race and gender, saying it is voluntary. I suspect the rate I get could depend on it even though they say otherwise. Do I fill it in or skip?
A coworker's public Instagram shows her on a beach during a day she called in sick. My manager asked the team, in a group chat, if anyone knew where she was. Do I say nothing, or tell the truth?

I moderate a hobby forum and a longtime member posted a how-to that quietly includes a link to pirated software. He's helped hundreds of people here. Do I remove the post and warn him, or leave it since the rest is useful?
I run a small newsletter and a source gave me documents on the condition I never name them. The documents themselves would identify them to anyone who knows the office. Do I publish anyway?
A moderator removed my comment in a local news group for 'misinformation' when I was citing my own experience at the clinic. I can appeal. Do I appeal or let it go and look like I was wrong?

I'm on a hiring panel and looked up a candidate's social media, where I found years-old posts that suggest a political view I disagree with but nothing about work. The policy says judge only on interviews. Do I mention what I saw to the panel?
My fitness app synced my runs to a public map that shows where I start from home. A follower commented on my street. Do I delete the history or just hide future routes?

My freelance client keeps adding scope in a shared doc and marking tasks 'urgent' on a Friday night, and the platform's rating system punishes slow responses. I need the rating for future work. Do I respond now or set a boundary?

I run our company's LinkedIn page and was told to delete a former employee's critical comment about how we handled a layoff. The comment is civil and factually accurate. Do I delete it to protect the brand, or leave it and explain to my boss why I did?
I found a public spreadsheet where a city contractor listed residents' disability status while processing permits. I'm not supposed to have access. Do I report it and reveal I was looking?

My workplace uses a recognition app where peers send points redeemable for gifts, and I noticed my manager giving all points to one favorite. I could say something to HR or let it go. What should I do?

I run the volunteer schedule for a food bank through a shared spreadsheet. A reliable volunteer asked me to hide her name from the public sign-up because of an ex. Doing so breaks the roster formula. How do I handle it?
My company is asking everyone to upload a short video introduction for a 'culture page' that will be public. I stammer and I'm job-hunting quietly. Do I submit one or ask for an exception?

My insurance portal now shows a 'wellness score' built from my step tracker, and a low score would bump my premium next year. I can unlink the tracker, but then the portal nags me daily. What should I do?

My apartment building switched to a package locker app, and a neighbor's medicine delivery got locked in my slot by mistake. The app has no way to reach them directly, and I know they need it tonight. What should I do?

A coworker keeps tagging me in a public team channel to 'confirm' decisions I was never part of. Each time I correct it, the thread resurfaces. My manager says it's just how he communicates. Do I keep correcting in public or move it to a private message?
I moderate a regional buy-nothing group. A member I know is reselling free items on a marketplace app, and she is the only one who picks up from a housebound elder. Do I ban her or warn her?
An online course I bought is now free to the public. I paid full price last month. Do I ask for a refund or let it go?

An online marketplace suspended my seller account after a buyer claimed the item never arrived. Tracking shows it did. The appeal form only lets me submit once. Do I write a calm appeal or attach the buyer's angry messages?

I admin a workplace Slack and saw, in a channel I wasn't meant to read, that my manager is planning to eliminate my role next quarter. Nobody knows I saw it. Do I start job hunting silently, or confront them?

I use a password manager my whole family shares, and I can see my teenager saved logins for sites I didn't know about. Nothing dangerous, but private. Do I say something or quietly create them their own vault?

My landlord uses a tenant-screening app that pulled a credit report with an old address I never lived at. I can dispute it, but the lease renewal is due Friday. Do I sign and dispute later or hold out?

My employer's internal directory now shows everyone's calendar and status, and I can see a manager blocking hours for 'interviews' with my teammates. No openings are posted. Do I ask my manager what's happening?

A charity I support emailed asking me to share their donation page on social media with a claim about impact that I know is overstated. They're doing good work otherwise. Do I share it anyway or ask them to correct it first?
My child's online tutor asked to move lessons to a personal video account instead of the platform, saying the fees are too high. It's cheaper but there's no record or protection. Do I agree?

A recruiter reached out on a job site using my current work email, which means someone at my company may see the thread. The role is a real step up. Do I reply from my personal account and risk looking evasive, or ignore it entirely?

My team's sprint board auto-assigns tickets to whoever last touched a file, and I got a P1 at 11pm because I fixed a typo there two years ago. Nobody set that rule on purpose. Do I quietly reassign it and let the board keep mislabeling everyone?
Our HR portal asks me to update my emergency contact, and the only person I trust is a coworker who would then be contacted before my family. Do I list her or keep my estranged brother?

Our team's standup bot posts everyone's task status publicly, and mine shows I'm behind because I'm covering for a sick teammate. My boss hasn't noticed yet. Do I add a note in the bot explaining why, or let the numbers speak?

My employer's AI assistant drafts my out-of-office replies and has been accepting meeting invites while I am on leave. I just noticed. Do I cancel the meetings myself or let them pile up for my return?
I received a message from a stranger on a genealogy site saying we are related and asking for my mother's maiden name to 'confirm the tree.' It could be genuine. Do I reply or ignore it?
I am on a community board reviewing grant applications, and one is from my cousin's nonprofit. The portal does not require disclosure. Do I recuse myself without saying why?

My company's expense app auto-fills 'client dinner' when I submit late meals, and everyone just approves them. Last week I genuinely ate alone while traveling. Editing it to the truth means my manager gets a flag and I look like the only one not doing it. What should I do?

My insurance portal shows a claim denied for a procedure I had, citing a diagnosis code that is not mine. The appeals form has a deadline of tomorrow and I cannot reach anyone by phone. Do I submit an appeal with guesses, or let it lapse?
My kid's school uses a parent portal that lists every family's unpaid lunch balances by name. I can see my neighbor is behind. I could quietly pay theirs through the portal. Should I, without asking?

A job candidate I interviewed asked me on LinkedIn, after being rejected, what they did wrong. The honest answer is that the team didn't like their communication style. Do I give the real feedback or a polite brush-off?
A hiring manager wants me to keep a rejection message warm by saying we 'found a better fit,' when we actually froze the role. The candidate is a former colleague. What do I write?

The pharmacy app let me schedule a refill but the pickup time conflicts with a shift I can't change, and there's no option to hold it past 48 hours. Missing it means starting over. Do I ask a neighbor or pay for delivery?

My landlord uses an online portal for maintenance requests, and I reported a mold issue that he marked 'resolved' without visiting. I have photos. Do I escalate through the portal again or post them in the building group chat?
A neighborhood app lets me report 'suspicious' cars, and a van has parked outside my house three nights running. The driver might be a night nurse. Do I post about it?
A recruiter messaged me on a job board asking me to confirm my current salary in writing before an interview. I know that will anchor the offer low. Do I share it, decline, or give a range?

An old friend from school found me online and wants to reconnect, but their feed is full of posts that suggest they've fallen into something I find alarming. Do I meet up, or keep it to messages and see?
A local news site asked readers to submit photos of flooding for a story. My photo shows a neighbor's car with a visible license plate. Do I submit it or crop the plate first?

I sold a bicycle online and the buyer now claims it was stolen from them before I sold it, based on a serial number they found. I bought it at a yard sale years ago. Do I refund them or stand my ground?

I am on a video call with a client when my partner walks in and says something about a deal they are negotiating with the same client. The client heard it. Do I pretend it did not happen or address it?

I am selling tickets to a concert online, and someone offered more than the listed price to jump the queue, paying through a cash app I do not use. It might be a scam but I need the money. What should I do?

Our school's parent portal shows my kid's grades to both me and my ex, and I can see my ex has been logging in daily. The custody agreement is silent on this. Do I ask the school to limit access or leave it?

Our patient portal lets me see my mother's lab results because I set up her account years ago with my email. She hasn't asked me to stop, but she also doesn't know I check. A result came back concerning and her doctor hasn't called yet. Do I tell her I saw it?

A colleague asked me to vote for their project in an online company contest, and I think another project is more deserving. The vote is public within the company. Do I vote honestly or support my colleague?

I moderate a neighborhood forum and a post naming a registered sex offender who just moved in has hundreds of replies, some with his address. It's legal to share in our state but my gut says remove it. Do I take it down and face the backlash?

I am a rideshare driver, and a passenger left a phone in my car. The app will not let me contact them without going through support, which takes hours. I could unlock it and call their emergency contact. Should I?

The scheduling tool booked me for a performance review with a manager who was laid off last week, and the slot is in an hour. HR says just show up and someone will cover. Do I attend and let a stranger run it, or ask to reschedule?
A friend running for a local office asked me to leave a glowing review of their campaign on a community site. I have not decided to support them. Do I write it, decline, or stay silent?

My gym's app tracks attendance and my employer's health plan offers a rebate for gym visits. I've been going less but the app keeps logging me in because of a glitch. Do I report the glitch or take the rebate?

A customer in our support forum posted their account number and a screenshot of their medical bill. I can delete it, but the thread is now public and indexed. Should I delete it and risk breaking the conversation, or leave it?

Our team uses a shared password vault, and I noticed a departing contractor's login still works. IT says deactivation is 'in the queue.' The contractor had access to client files. Do I wait for IT or change it myself?

Our team uses an AI meeting notetaker that joins every call, and a colleague just disclosed a pregnancy on a call before realizing it was recording. Do I delete that segment or leave the record intact?

My employer's AI assistant drafted an email to a client that contains a detail from another client's file. I caught it before sending. Do I report the bug and expose my usage, or just fix it and move on?
I run a small newsletter and a reader sent a tip that would embarrass a local official but I cannot verify it. Publishing could be wrong; sitting on it feels like protecting power. What do I do?

The grocery delivery app keeps substituting items I'm allergic to, and I flagged it twice. The last driver said the store's system overrides customer notes. Do I keep ordering or switch and lose my credits?
A local news site's comment section is attacking a librarian by name, and I know her. Reporting each comment feels endless. Do I write a public defense or stay out of it?

My online therapy platform matched me with a counselor who is also a parent at my child's school. Switching means a six-week wait. Do I stay and pretend we have never met, or switch and delay my care?

I'm on a job search and my current employer's HR uses the same recruiting platform where I have a profile marked 'open to work.' I can hide it, but a recruiter I know says hiding makes me invisible. What do I do?
A rideshare driver's profile photo doesn't match the person who showed up, and the app says the account is verified. I got home safely but I'm uneasy. Do I report it now or let it go?

My company's travel booking site offers a cheaper flight with a longer layover that would make me miss my daughter's recital. My manager said pick the cheaper one. Do I book the expensive one and explain?
My company's calendar tool now shows everyone's focus time, and mine is empty most days because I take meetings. My manager hinted I should block time to look disciplined. Do I block fake focus time?

A local news site's comment section is spreading a rumor that a teacher at my kid's school was fired for something serious. I happen to know it's a budget cut. Do I post what I know, or stay out of it?

Our team's project tracker auto-assigns tasks to whoever last touched a ticket. I keep getting work that belongs to someone on leave, and the deadline is real. Do I reassign it and risk the system flagging me, or quietly do it and let someone else get credit?
A coworker I supervise asked me on a private channel to cover for him because he's interviewing elsewhere. I want to be loyal to him but I also report to the same manager. What do I say?

The telehealth intake form asks whether I have ever felt unsafe at home. I do sometimes, but my partner is in the room and could see the screen. Do I answer truthfully online or wait for an in-person visit?

My kid's school app sends real-time location during field trips, and other parents are sharing the live link in a group chat that includes people I don't know. Do I say something to the school or the chat?
My city's 311 app let me report a pothole, and a neighbor says I am wasting city time because it is on private land. The app already dispatched a crew. Do I cancel the report or let it go?

A group chat for my hobby club is planning a meetup at a bar I know a member was banned from for harassment. The organizers do not know. Do I tell them privately or let it go?
My kid's online tutor keeps texting me after hours about non-tutoring topics. Nothing explicitly wrong, but it feels off. Do I say something to the tutoring company or handle it myself?

My aging father's bank keeps texting me alerts because I am his authorized contact. He asked me to stop reading them and just tell him if something is wrong. I saw a charge I think is a scam. Do I tell him?

I found a public database that lists my home address alongside my voter registration. I can request removal, but the form requires me to upload my ID, which feels like more exposure. Do I submit the ID or leave it?

I run the church's volunteer signup site and can see everyone's phone numbers and emails. A member asked me for another volunteer's number for a surprise. Do I share it or relay a message instead?
A coworker I manage asked me to connect on a social app, and their profile shows political posts that would change how our director sees them. I already accepted. Do I unfollow quietly or leave it?

Our book club moved to a video app that records sessions for absent members. A member shared something personal last week. Should I ask the host to delete that recording?
A stranger on a forum asked me to share a file for a project we both work on. The file has a coworker's personal notes in the margins. Do I strip them first or just send it?
Our landlord switched rent payments to an app that charges a fee for card but not bank transfer, and my bank account is nearly empty until Friday. Do I pay the fee or risk lateness?

My therapy app offered a discounted annual plan if I let it share anonymized mood data with researchers. The fine print says 'anonymized' but asks for my zip code and employer. Should I take the discount?

A former professor posted a public fundraiser for medical bills, and I suspect some details are exaggerated based on what I know. I don't want to accuse anyone. Do I donate quietly or ask questions?

My employer posted a job opening identical to mine with a higher salary range. I saw it on the public careers page. Do I apply, ask my manager, or quietly look elsewhere?
A stranger on a local forum posted a photo of a lost dog that looks exactly like mine, and the phone number is wrong. I can comment publicly or message the poster privately. Which?

My elderly neighbor asked me to set up her online banking, and while doing it I saw her account balance is far lower than she thinks. She's mentioned a nephew who 'helps' with money. Do I tell her what I saw?

My apartment's package room uses an app that photographs every delivery, and I can see my neighbor's medical supply boxes in the shared feed. Do I tell the building or mind my business?

A close friend sent me a link to a petition that names a local official I know is being harassed. I agree with the petition's goal but not the tactic. Do I sign, stay silent, or tell her why I am not signing?

My daughter's school uses a behavior app that pushes alerts to my phone whenever she talks in class. She asked me to stop checking it. Do I keep monitoring?

I found a public spreadsheet where a hospital left patient appointment times visible without names. Reporting it might get a friend who works there in trouble. Do I report it?

A friend asked me to 'like and share' her small business page from my account, which is mostly coworkers and family. I want to help but it feels like a public endorsement. Do I share it or just like it?

I am a volunteer for a mutual aid group, and a request for help came from someone whose profile looks newly created and vague. Others are donating. Do I ask for more verification publicly or trust it?

A former coworker asked me for a LinkedIn recommendation and I'd have to stretch the truth about how closely we worked. She's struggling to find work. Do I write something warm but vague, decline, or tell her why?
